key_insight: AUTOPILOT-VQA introduces a benchmark designed to test whether vision-language models can understand safety-critical incidents in dashcam videos, not just describe scenes. It focuses on incident-centric reasoning, making evaluation closer to real-world autonomous driving needs.
problem_solved: Current vision-language benchmarks do not reliably measure whether models can reason about dangerous or incident-related events in driving videos. This paper addresses the gap by creating a dedicated evaluation setup for dashcam incident understanding.
method: Builds AUTOPILOT-VQA, an incident-centric visual question answering benchmark for dashcam video understanding.
Frames evaluation around safety-critical incidents to test model reasoning, not only object or scene recognition.
Uses question-answer pairs over driving videos to assess how well multimodal models understand events relevant to autonomous driving safety.
impact: This benchmark helps researchers and engineers evaluate multimodal models on realistic driving safety tasks. It can guide the development of more reliable autonomous driving systems that better detect and reason about incidents.

paper_title: AUTOPILOT VQA: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Incident-Centric Dashcam Understanding
paper_authors: Siddharth Damodharan, Radhika Gupta, Ali Alshami, Ryan Rabinowitz, Jugal Kalita
